subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicit `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys bypass the soft credential-name block for host exec inheritance when hard dangerous-host env blocks still win?
rationale: The source-level fix is small, but it defines which operator-configured secrets may enter subprocess environments and therefore needs maintainer security-boundary intent.

options.title: Allow explicit skill env keys
options.body: Treat keys explicitly listed in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-approved soft-sensitive overrides, while keeping `NODE_OPTIONS`, loader hooks, shell startup hooks, and similar hard blocks unbypassable.

options.title: Require skill metadata declarations
options.body: Keep the current behavior and require skills to declare every credential-shaped env key in `primaryEnv` or `requires.env`, then update docs and diagnostics.

options.title: Move secrets outside skill env
options.body: Declare per-skill credential env injection unsupported for credential-shaped keys and direct users to host process env, SecretRef-backed config, or plugin-owned auth flows.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit skill env keys
recommendation.body: Treat keys explicitly listed in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as operator-approved soft-sensitive overrides, while keeping `NODE_OPTIONS`, loader hooks, shell startup hooks, and similar hard blocks unbypassable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work on sensitive skill env allowlisting and sandbox env security makes this the strongest available routing signal.
